findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing or unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and use .map_err(|e| IoError::Read { path: path.to_owned(), source: e }) or similar typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric second field or missing field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (missing column or non-numeric value) aborts the program instead of returning a typed Parse or Invalid error
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) and .map_err(|_| ParseError::Parse) on the parse call

findings.problem: lossy as u16 cast after parse — values > 65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value outside u16 range silently wraps to an incorrect value, producing corrupt domain data with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line with no comma causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to safely extract name and value parts

findings.problem: println! hidden I/O side effect inside data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: pure data parsing has observable side effects, preventing deterministic testing and introducing logging into the data pipeline
findings.fix: remove println! or pass a sink/callback abstraction; the core parsing path must be side-effect free

findings.problem: load_metrics mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), and parsing in one function with no typed error boundary
findings.failure_mode: cannot independently test the pure parsing logic; I/O failures, parse failures, and truncation all collapse into a Vec with panics as the only error signal
findings.fix: split into: (1) a pure fn parse_records(iter_of_str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>; (2) a shell fn load_metrics(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> that reads, maps I/O errors, and delegates to the pure core

findings.problem: Record.name is a bare String with no domain constraint; value is u16 but parsed from u32 with lossy cast
findings.failure_mode: any string is a valid name (including empty or whitespace); value has no compile-time guarantee of being in-range for the domain
findings.fix: introduce Name newtype with a fallible constructor that rejects empty/whitespace; use u16-parse or checked conversion with typed error

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocated for every line split with no capacity hint or try_reserve
findings.failure_mode: large input files cause unbounded per-line allocations; allocation failure is not part of the error contract
findings.fix: use split_once and parse in-place without collecting into Vec; if Vec is needed, call try_reserve before pushing and map Allocation error

findings.problem: No domain error type exists; all failures are communicated via panic
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot handle specific failure modes (missing file, invalid CSV, out-of-range value, allocation failure)
findings.fix: define a sealed error enum: pub enum MetricsError { Io(IoError), Invalid(line: usize), Overflow(line: usize), Allocation }; return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricsError>

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_metrics
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify whether the function meets latency or throughput requirements; intermediate Vec allocations are unmeasured
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring bytes read, allocations, and wall time across realistic file sizes; run with --bench and report results

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data (perf, flamegraph, or alloc counters) for the parsing path
no allocation evidence (no try_reserve, no capacity budget)
no second-ring evidence (no formal spec, no property tests, no Kani/Verus proofs)
no command-level evidence (no recorded cargo test/cargo bench/cargo clippy run)
residual_risk: The entire function panics on any malformed input, missing file, or out-of-range value. There is no typed error domain, no functional core separation, no bounded allocation, and no performance evidence. This crate is not delivery-ready for any production or high-assurance context.
